title: LLM-Anthropic 0.31 Plugin Adds Prompt Caching Support
summary: Simon Willison's LLM-Anthropic plugin version 0.31 now supports prompt caching for Claude models, reducing API costs and improving performance.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Simon Willison released LLM-Anthropic 0.31 on November 9, 2026, adding prompt caching support for Claude API users.
- Prompt caching reduces API costs by up to 90% and speeds up responses when reusing conversation context across requests.
- The plugin integrates with Willison's LLM command-line tool, making Claude models accessible via terminal with cost-efficient caching.


Developer Simon Willison officially released LLM-Anthropic version 0.31 on November 9, 2026, introducing prompt caching support for Anthropic's Claude models. The update enables command-line users to dramatically reduce API costs and improve response times when working with Claude through repeated conversations or iterative workflows.


## What Prompt Caching Delivers


Prompt caching allows the plugin to store and reuse portions of conversation context across multiple API requests. When users continue a conversation or work with the same system prompt repeatedly, cached content bypasses the standard token processing pipeline. According to Anthropic's pricing structure, cached tokens cost 90% less than standard input tokens, translating to substantial savings for developers running extended sessions or batch operations.


The feature proves particularly valuable for workflows involving large system prompts, extensive documentation context, or multi-turn conversations where earlier messages remain relevant. Response latency drops significantly because the model skips reprocessing cached segments, focusing computational resources only on new input.


## Release Date and Integration


Officially released on November 9, 2026, version 0.31 integrates seamlessly with Willison's existing LLM command-line tool ecosystem. Users can upgrade via pip and immediately access caching functionality without modifying their existing scripts or workflows. The plugin maintains backward compatibility with earlier versions while exposing new caching parameters through command-line flags.


Installation requires Python 3.8 or later and an active Anthropic API key. The plugin supports all current Claude model variants, including Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3 Opus, with automatic cache management handled behind the scenes.


## Developer Workflow Impact


Command-line developers gain several practical advantages from the caching implementation. Iterative prompt engineering sessions become more cost-effective, as refined variations build on cached base prompts rather than reprocessing identical context. Code review workflows that analyze multiple files against the same coding standards see immediate cost reductions. Documentation generation tasks that reference large codebases benefit from caching the project context while varying specific queries.


- Up to 90% cost reduction on cached input tokens versus standard processing
- Faster response times through bypassed reprocessing of cached segments
- Automatic cache management with no manual cache invalidation required
- Full compatibility with existing LLM tool configurations and scripts


## Technical Implementation


The plugin leverages Anthropic's native prompt caching API endpoints, exposing cache control through intuitive command-line parameters. Developers can specify cache breakpoints within their prompts, designating which segments should persist across requests. The system automatically tracks cache expiration based on Anthropic's five-minute timeout window, refreshing cached content as needed without user intervention.


Willison's implementation prioritizes developer experience, abstracting complex caching logic into simple flags while maintaining full access to advanced configuration options for power users. The plugin logs cache hit rates and token savings, providing transparency into cost optimization achieved through each session.


## What This Means


LLM-Anthropic 0.31 removes a significant friction point for developers building with Claude models through command-line interfaces. By reducing both cost and latency for iterative workflows, the plugin makes sophisticated AI integration more accessible to individual developers and small teams operating on constrained budgets. The update positions Willison's LLM tool as an increasingly practical bridge between Anthropic's powerful models and the developer workflows where cost efficiency directly impacts project viability.
